advances: An arbitrary positive multiplier on all the child blocks of one full rooted spine admits an absolute original cubic-depth moment bound. The number of strong blocks is the full tree depth \(Q\). First-divergence classes have summable fourth-moment capacities because each prescribed spine direction has probability at most \(1-\eta\). The root-divergent class retains the actual cross-level halfspace geometry while preserving the entire spine label.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. Accepted fact 032423921efad6c8 supplies the original chain/tree support, unique sources, and inverse reconstruction. Accepted fact 604889294a17d7df supplies the exact log-affine height support and parameter estimates. Accepted fact 09eb292dfb337c81 supplies the directional rarity estimate. Accepted fact b9989d13ba245ea2 supplies the path-variation normalization, full Boolean-normalizer convention, and height-sum bound. Accepted fact d9c4b095a13caaba supplies the actual neighbor-and-endpoint halfspace selection and its scalar height estimates. The spine partition, enlarged-label census, full conditional normalizers, rare-anchor estimates, summable capacities, and transfer are proved here.
proof:
Write \(P_\lambda=\Pi(\lambda)\), \(\eta=1-2^{-m}\binom m{m/2}\), and \(\delta=1-\eta\). Accepted facts 032423921efad6c8 and 604889294a17d7df give
$$
Q\ge4,\qquad 0<\delta<(Q+1)^{-2},\qquad\eta^Q>\frac34.
\tag{1}
$$
Their unique-source property recovers the Boolean source of a spatial point by reduction modulo two, and its twos give its forward prefix. All parameters and supports below retain exactly these predecessor meanings.

For a local direction \(i\), put
$$
\vartheta_i=2^{-m}|\lbrace c\in D_m:i_m(c)=i\rbrace|.
$$
The directional estimate of accepted fact 09eb292dfb337c81 is
$$
0<\vartheta_i\le\delta,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{m}\vartheta_i=\eta.
\tag{2}
$$
Indeed, there are \(2^m\delta\) symmetric chains, and each adds a given direction at most once. The chain containing the empty set runs through every rank to the full set and adds every direction once, proving positivity. Thus (2) holds for every permitted chain partition. Write \(v_r=v_{r-1}i_r\) for the fixed spine directions.

Partition the spatial support as follows. For \(0\le j\le Q\), let \(\mathrm{STOP}_j\) consist of points of level exactly \(j\) whose selected coordinates are \(v_1,\ldots,v_j\). For \(0\le j<Q\), let \(\mathrm{BRANCH}_j\) consist of points of level at least \(j+1\) whose selected coordinates begin \(v_1,\ldots,v_j\), with the next selected coordinate different from \(v_{j+1}\). Every spatial point belongs to exactly one of these sets: either its entire finite selected prefix lies on the spine, or it has a unique first divergence. The word STOP describes the spatial point's level and does not require its Boolean source to fail its next test.

Lift each of these classes to \(\widehat A\) by retaining every original height in each of its columns. For any lifted class \(E\), let \(\nu_E\) be the restriction of the actual weighted measure to \(E\), let \(W_E=\nu_E(\mathbb R^N)\), and put \(p^E=\nu_E/W_E\). Define \(\tau_{p^E}\) using the same family of closed halfspaces of \(\mathbb R^N\). All these classes are nonempty: the prescribed directions have positive counts by (2), and the divergence test has positive probability \(\eta-\vartheta_{i_{j+1}}\ge1-2\delta>0\). Their weights and normalizers are therefore positive.

We use repeatedly that an atom belongs to every halfspace containing it. Consequently, for any such restricted law,
$$
M_3(p^E)\ge W_E^{-4}\sum_{\mathbf I\in E}w_{\mathbf I}^4.
\tag{3}
$$
For positive numbers \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\), we also use
$$
\sum_{r=1}^{M}x_r^4\ge M^{-3}\left(\sum_{r=1}^{M}x_r\right)^4.
\tag{4}
$$

The disjoint block census for a prescribed spine prefix gives
$$
M_j:=|\mathrm{STOP}_j|
=2^n\prod_{r=1}^{j}\vartheta_{i_r}
\le2^n\delta^j.
\tag{5}
$$
For this count each of the \(j\) fixed blocks has \(2^m\vartheta_{i_r}\) permissible source patterns, and all other source bits are free. The fixed-level source map is injective by parity. The empty product is one, so (5) includes \(j=0\). All columns of this class have entrance \(a_j\). If \(L_j=\sum_{z\in\mathrm{STOP}_j}f(z|_S)e^{\lambda\cdot z}\), their full normalizer is at most \(2^{1-a_j}L_j\). Apply (3) only to their actual atoms at height \(a_j\), then apply (4). This proves
$$
M_3(p^{\widehat{\mathrm{STOP}}_j})
\ge\frac1{16M_j^3}
\ge8^{-n}\frac{\delta^{-3j}}{16}.
\tag{6}
$$
This also covers \(j=Q\), including its possibly single-height columns.

For \(0\le j<Q\), let \(\mathcal B_j\subseteq\mathrm{BRANCH}_j\) be its level-\((j+1)\) anchors. The same disjoint block census gives
$$
|\mathcal B_j|
=2^n\left(\prod_{r=1}^{j}\vartheta_{i_r}\right)
 (\eta-\vartheta_{i_{j+1}})
\le2^n\delta^j.
\tag{7}
$$
Once a path diverges at depth \(j+1\), every later visited node is off the fixed spine, and its child block is disjoint from \(S\). Thus, for every source producing a point of this branch at level \(s\ge j+1\), the source's anchor \(z_{j+1}(b)\) has exactly the same restriction to \(S\) as \(z_s(b)\). In particular, the arbitrary multiplier is exactly equal at the two points. The additional spikes multiply the exponential factor by at most \(e^{2P_\lambda}\). For each fixed \(s\), the map to anchors is injective because the anchor recovers the full Boolean source by parity.

Put \(L_j^{\mathrm b}=\sum_{z\in\mathcal B_j}f(z|_S)e^{\lambda\cdot z}\). At each of the \(Q-j\) possible levels, the spatial weight sum is at most \(e^{2P_\lambda}L_j^{\mathrm b}\). All their entrance heights are at least \(a_{j+1}\), so the full branch normalizer obeys
$$
W_{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j}
\le2e^{2P_\lambda}L_j^{\mathrm b}(Q-j)2^{-a_{j+1}}.
\tag{8}
$$
The actual anchor atoms at height \(a_{j+1}\), (3), (4), and (7) therefore give
$$
M_3(p^{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j})
\ge\frac{e^{-8P_\lambda}}{16|\mathcal B_j|^3(Q-j)^4}
\ge8^{-n}\frac{e^{-8}\delta^{-3j}}{16(Q-j)^4}.
\tag{9}
$$
We use this estimate only for \(1\le j<Q\). It has no uncontrolled multiplier ratio and includes all branch columns in its denominator.

It remains to give a uniform estimate for the root-divergent class \(E_*=\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_0\). Its allowable \(S\)-labels form the set
$$
\mathcal L=\left\lbrace\sigma:
 \sigma[v_0]=c+2e_{i_m(c)},\ c\in D_m,\ i_m(c)\ne i_1;
 \quad\sigma_u\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace\ (u\in S\setminus\lbrace1,\ldots,m\rbrace)
\right\rbrace.
\tag{10}
$$
Here the root-child block is indexed by the words of length one. Every label in (10) occurs at level one with every Boolean assignment outside \(S\). Conversely, every root-divergent point has such a label, because all its later selected coordinates lie outside \(S\). The recovered root source pattern and all the later fixed spine blocks specify the label uniquely. In particular,
$$
0<|\mathcal L|
=2^{mQ}(\eta-\vartheta_{i_1})\le2^{mQ}.
\tag{11}
$$
The injectivity in this equality is the source recovery \(c+2e_{i_m(c)}\mapsto c\), replacing its unique two by zero. All labels are in \(R_S\), so \(f\) is defined and positive on them.

For every field \(\theta\) vanishing on \(S\), define the restricted Boolean product and its full counterpart by
$$
Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}=\prod_{u\in\mathcal T_{m,Q}\setminus S}(1+e^{\theta_u}),
\qquad
Z_\theta=\prod_{u\in\mathcal T_{m,Q}}(1+e^{\theta_u})
=2^{mQ}Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}.
\tag{12}
$$
The latter \(Z_\theta\) is exactly the full Boolean normalizer of accepted fact b9989d13ba245ea2. Only the outside product is used in the following conditional census and normalizers. Put
$$
\mathfrak f_1=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L}f(\sigma),
\qquad\mathfrak f_4=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L}f(\sigma)^4.
$$
By (4), (11), and \( (1+x)^4\le8(1+x^4)\),
$$
\frac{\mathfrak f_4}{\mathfrak f_1^4}\ge8^{-mQ},
\qquad
\frac{Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}}{(Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}})^4}
\ge8^{-(n-mQ)}.
\tag{13}
$$
The second inequality multiplies the displayed two-term fourth-power inequality over precisely the \(n-mQ\) coordinates outside \(S\). The product of the two ratios in (13) is thus at least \(8^{-n}\), independently of the number of labels or the values of \(f\).

At every level \(s\ge1\) and fixed label \(\sigma\in\mathcal L\), source recovery injects that level's points into all Boolean assignments outside \(S\). The label already fixes its root source and all source bits in \(S\). The root spike has zero field, and the other spikes cost at most \(e^{2P_\lambda}\). Dropping only the forward-success restrictions therefore gives the full normalizer bound
$$
W_{E_*}\le e^{2P_\lambda}\mathfrak f_1Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}}R_k^+,
\qquad
R_k^+=\sum_{s=1}^{Q}\sum_{t=a_s}^{k}2^{-t}\le R_k
\le\frac{9+\log k}{4}.
\tag{14}
$$
Here \(R_k=\sum_{s=0}^{Q}\sum_{t=a_s}^{k}2^{-t}\) is exactly the height sum in accepted fact b9989d13ba245ea2. The estimate also follows directly from geometric tails:

$$
R_k\le2+2\sum_{\ell=8}^{k}b_\ell2^{-\ell}
\le2+\frac{H_k-H_7}{4}\le\frac{9+\log k}{4}.
$$

For \(1\le s\le Q\), let \(\mathcal C_s(\sigma)\) be the complete level-\(s\) points of this label, meaning that their canonical inverse reconstruction continues through depth \(Q\). We claim the following census for every field \(\theta\) zero on \(S\):
$$
\sum_{z\in\mathcal C_s(\sigma)}e^{\theta\cdot z}
\ge\eta^{Q-1}e^{-3\Pi(\theta)}Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}.
\tag{15}
$$
To prove it, fix the root source pattern recovered from \(\sigma[v_0]\). Its first selected child differs from \(v_1\). Give every coordinate outside \(S\) independent Boolean product law with normalizer \(Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}\). Beginning at that selected root child, require \(s-1\) forward \(D_m\) tests, followed by \(Q-s\) inverse \(\operatorname{im}F_m\) tests. Every one of these \(Q-1\) blocks is outside \(S\), fresh, and disjoint from all other revealed blocks. The fixed later spine labels impose no condition on them.

Under fair outside bits the total success probability is exactly \(\eta^{Q-1}\), since both tested pattern sets have fraction \(\eta\). A successful adaptive transcript fixes exactly its visited blocks and leaves all other outside bits free. The transcripts are disjoint: their first different pattern occurs at the same node, which their common earlier patterns determine. Under the product law, the probability ratio for a specified bit \(b_u\) relative to a fair bit is
$$
\frac{2e^{\theta_ub_u}}{1+e^{\theta_u}}\ge e^{-|\theta_u|}.
$$
The ratio of each successful transcript is consequently at least \(e^{-\Pi(\theta)}\); its blocks lie on one rooted path and the omitted root block has zero field. Summing over these disjoint transcripts gives success probability at least \(e^{-\Pi(\theta)}\eta^{Q-1}\).

On success, form the spatial point by making the first \(s\) selected zeros into twos, including the already fixed root spike. This gives a bijection onto \(\mathcal C_s(\sigma)\): parity recovers the full source, and forward-prefix and injective inverse-suffix reconstruction recover the transcript. The spike factor is at least \(e^{-2\Pi(\theta)}\). Multiplying the preceding probability lower bound by this factor and \(Z_\theta^{\mathrm{out}}\) proves (15). This argument proves the census with the enlarged immutable labels directly; it does not identify the pinned support with a smaller original tree.

Suppose first \(k\ge2^{16}\). Put \(L=\log k\), \(g=\lfloor\sqrt{k}\rfloor\). The scalar estimates in accepted fact d9c4b095a13caaba are
$$
L>9,\qquad
U_k:=\sum_{\ell=8}^{g}b_\ell2^{-\ell}\ge\frac L{32},
\qquad R_k\le\frac L2.
\tag{16}
$$
Sample the actual original indices
$$
\mathcal G_*=\left\lbrace(z,a_s+1):
 z\in\mathcal C_s(\sigma),\ \sigma\in\mathcal L,\quad8\le a_s\le g
\right\rbrace.
$$
Every such height is in its original column. For such a complete \(z\), write its inverse continuation as \(u_{s+1},\ldots,u_Q\), and set \(V_r=\sum_{q=s+1}^{r}e_{u_q}\). The actual-halfspace mechanism of accepted fact d9c4b095a13caaba selects, in every containing closed ambient halfspace at \(\mathbf I=(z,a_s+1)\), distinct original indices of total untilted weight at least \(L/128\), all of the forms
$$
(z-e_{u_r},a_s),\qquad
(z-V_r,a_r),\qquad(z+V_r,a_r),\qquad r>s.
\tag{17}
$$
These are the same points, heights, and normalization as in that predecessor. The inverse reconstruction gives the endpoint levels \(s,r\); changing a single suffix one to zero leaves the first \(s\) forward blocks intact, proving that the neighbors also have level \(s\).

For completeness, the halfspace selection uses no mass outside this displayed family. For a halfspace through \(\mathbf I\) with nonnegative height coefficient, at least one endpoint in (17) is included for each \(a_r\ge2g\). Their total weight is at least \(L/32\), by the scalar estimate \(\sum_{\ell=2g}^{k}b_\ell2^{-\ell}\ge L/32\) in accepted fact d9c4b095a13caaba. With a negative height coefficient \(-\beta\), \(\beta>0\), call \(r\) bad if its spatial coefficient \(c_{u_r}\le\beta\). Every bad lower neighbor is included. Either these neighbors already have total weight at least \(L/128\), or there are fewer than \(2^{a_s}L/128\) bad indices. In the latter case, successive normalized endpoint partial sums have increments greater than one between bad indices. At most \(4k2^gL\) of these partial sums can lie in \([-k,k]\). All remaining endpoints with \(a_r\ge2g\) contribute one included point. The discarded mass is at most \(4k2^{-g}L\le L/64\), leaving at least \(L/64\). These bounds hold because \(g\ge256\), \(2^g\ge256k\), and \(a_s\le g\), exactly as in the cited proof. A containing halfspace contains a parallel halfspace through the sampled point.

Crucially, all suffix nodes in (17) lie in the subtree of the root child different from \(v_1\). Every changed coordinate is outside \(S\). All selected points therefore retain the entire label \(\sigma=z|_S\), remain root-divergent, and have exactly the same multiplier \(f(\sigma)\). Their spatial displacements change coordinates on the complete rooted path by one in absolute value. Their field factors are at least \(e^{\lambda\cdot z-P_\lambda}\). It follows for the actual restricted unnormalized depth that
$$
h_{\nu_{E_*}}(z,a_s+1)
:=W_{E_*}\tau_{p^{E_*}}(z,a_s+1)
\ge f(\sigma)e^{\lambda\cdot z-P_\lambda}\frac L{128}.
\tag{18}
$$
This estimate allows every original ambient halfspace, including those whose restrictions to a label slice are constant.

Sum (18) under the restricted law, keeping its fourth normalizer. Apply (15) at \(\theta=4\lambda\), for which \(\Pi(4\lambda)=4P_\lambda\). Then (1), (14), and (16) give
$$
\begin{aligned}
M_3(p^{E_*})
&\ge\frac{e^{-3P_\lambda}L^3}{128^3W_{E_*}^4}
 \sum_{s:\,8\le a_s\le g}2^{-(a_s+1)}
 \sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal L}f(\sigma)^4
 \sum_{z\in\mathcal C_s(\sigma)}e^{4\lambda\cdot z}\\
&\ge\frac{\eta^{Q-1}e^{-15P_\lambda}
 \mathfrak f_4Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}U_kL^3}
 {2\cdot128^3W_{E_*}^4}\\
&\ge3\cdot2^{-25}e^{-23P_\lambda}
 \frac{\mathfrak f_4}{\mathfrak f_1^4}
 \frac{Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}}{(Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}})^4}
\ge3\cdot2^{-25}e^{-23}8^{-n}
>2^{-63}8^{-n}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
$$
For the last numerical inequality, \(e^{23}<3^{23}<2^{37}\), since \(3^5<2^8\) and \(3^3<2^5\). The exponential cost \(23P_\lambda\) consists of \(12P_\lambda\) from the fourth-field census, \(3P_\lambda\) from the cubed depth, and \(8P_\lambda\) from the fourth normalizer.

If \(8\le k<2^{16}\), then \(R_k<8\) by (14). Since \(b_8=4\), \(a_1=8\). For every \(\sigma\in\mathcal L\) and every outside Boolean assignment, the level-one point with this label has an actual atom at height eight. The exact sum of fourth powers of these atom weights is \(2^{-32}\mathfrak f_4Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}\); the field on \(S\) is zero. Thus (3), (13), and (14) yield
$$
M_3(p^{E_*})
>2^{-44}e^{-8P_\lambda}
 \frac{\mathfrak f_4}{\mathfrak f_1^4}
 \frac{Z_{4\lambda}^{\mathrm{out}}}{(Z_\lambda^{\mathrm{out}})^4}
\ge2^{-44}e^{-8}8^{-n}
>2^{-63}8^{-n},
\tag{20}
$$
using \(e^8<3^8<2^{13}\). Combining both height ranges, the root-divergent class has conditional moment at least \(8^{-n}\kappa_*\), where \(\kappa_*=2^{-63}\).

We now transfer all conditional bounds to the full original law. For every lifted class \(E\), put \(\alpha_E=W_E/W\); the classes are disjoint and exhaustive, so their positive \(\alpha_E\) sum to one. For a sampled index of \(E\), every containing halfspace has full \(p\)-mass at least \(\alpha_E\) times its \(p^E\)-mass. Taking infima over the same ambient halfspaces gives \(\tau_p\ge\alpha_E\tau_{p^E}\), while \(p=\alpha_Ep^E\) on \(E\). Consequently
$$
M_3(p)\ge\sum_E\alpha_E^4M_3(p^E)
\ge8^{-n}\sum_E\kappa_E\alpha_E^4,
\tag{21}
$$
where (6), (9), (19), and (20) permit the choices
$$
\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{STOP}}_j}=\frac{\delta^{-3j}}{16},\qquad
\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j}
=\frac{e^{-8}\delta^{-3j}}{16(Q-j)^4}\ (1\le j<Q),\qquad
\kappa_*=2^{-63}.
$$
Hölder's inequality, applied to \(\sum_E\alpha_E=1\), gives
$$
1\le\left(\sum_E\kappa_E\alpha_E^4\right)^{1/4}
 \left(\sum_E\kappa_E^{-1/3}\right)^{3/4}.
\tag{22}
$$
The capacities in the second factor are uniformly summable. Indeed, (1) and \(Q\ge4\) imply \(\delta<1/25\), so
$$
\sum_{j=0}^{Q}\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{STOP}}_j}^{-1/3}
\le\frac{16^{1/3}}{1-\delta}<3.
\tag{23}
$$
For example, \(16^{1/3}<8/3\) makes the last expression less than \(25/9<3\). For the nonroot branches,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j=1}^{Q-1}\kappa_{\widehat{\mathrm{BRANCH}}_j}^{-1/3}
&\le16^{1/3}e^{8/3}Q^{4/3}\frac{\delta}{1-\delta}\\
&<16^{1/3}e^{8/3}\frac{Q^{4/3}}{Q^2+2Q}<81.
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
$$
Here \(Q^{4/3}<Q^2+2Q\), \(16^{1/3}<3\), and \(e^{8/3}<e^3<27\). Finally \(\kappa_*^{-1/3}=2^{21}\). Thus
$$
\sum_E\kappa_E^{-1/3}<2^{21}+84<2^{22}.
$$
Equations (21) and (22) now prove
$$
M_3(p)>2^{-66}8^{-n}=2^{-63}8^{-N}\ge2^{-100}8^{-N}.
$$
The partition was used only for this exact fourth-power transfer. Every conditional normalizer included every original height of every spatial point of its class, and the classes together recover the full original \(W\) and \(p\). The arbitrary multiplier was preserved exactly in the branch transports and halfspace selections. No assertion of a uniform global density ratio or of a pinned smaller-tree identification was used.
statement:
Fix any integer \(k\ge8\), and use exactly the profile \(\rho_t=2^{-t}\) and support of accepted fact 604889294a17d7df, with the tree of accepted fact 032423921efad6c8. More explicitly, set
$$
b_\ell=0\ (1\le\ell<8),\qquad
b_\ell=\left\lfloor\frac{2^\ell}{8\ell}\right\rfloor\ (8\le\ell\le k),\qquad
Q_0=0,\quad Q_\ell=\sum_{r=1}^{\ell}b_r,\quad Q=Q_k,
$$
$$
m=2(Q+1)^4,\qquad n=\sum_{r=1}^{Q}m^r,\qquad N=n+1.
$$
Put \(a_0=0\), and put \(a_s=\ell\) when \(Q_{\ell-1}<s\le Q_\ell\). Thus \(k\) is the height parameter, \(Q\) is tree depth, \(m\) is branching number, and \(n\) is spatial dimension.

Choose any symmetric saturated chain partition of \(\lbrace0,1\rbrace^m\). Let \(D_m\) be its nonterminal vectors and \(F_m(c)=c+e_{i_m(c)}\) its injective successor. Index spatial coordinates by
$$
\mathcal T_{m,Q}=\bigcup_{r=1}^{Q}\lbrace1,\ldots,m\rbrace^r.
$$
For a node \(v\) of depth less than \(Q\), including the root \(\varnothing\), write \(z[v]=(z_{v1},\ldots,z_{vm})\) for its child-coordinate block. For a Boolean source \(b\), its forward path starts at the root and, at a node \(u\), continues to \(ui_m(b[u])\) if \(b[u]\in D_m\). Write \(h(b)\) for the path length and \(u_1,\ldots,u_{h(b)}\) for its selected coordinates. Retain the exact supports
$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{m,Q}&=\left\lbrace z_s(b)=b+2\sum_{r=1}^{s}e_{u_r}:
 b\in\lbrace0,1\rbrace^{\mathcal T_{m,Q}},\quad0\le s\le h(b)\right\rbrace,\\
\widehat A&=\left\lbrace(z,t):z\in A_{m,Q},\quad
 a_{\operatorname{level}(z)}\le t\le k,\quad t\in\mathbb Z\right\rbrace.
\end{aligned}
$$
The level of \(z_s(b)\) is \(s\), equivalently its number of coordinates equal to two.

Fix any full rooted spine \(v_0=\varnothing,v_1,\ldots,v_Q\), where \(v_{r+1}\) is a child of \(v_r\). Define the coordinate set
$$
S=\bigcup_{r=0}^{Q-1}\lbrace v_ri:1\le i\le m\rbrace,
\qquad |S|=mQ,\qquad
R_S=\lbrace z|_S:z\in A_{m,Q}\rbrace.
$$
Let \(f:R_S\longrightarrow(0,\infty)\) be arbitrary. Let \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^n\) vanish on \(S\), and assume
$$
\Pi(\lambda)=\max_{u_0,\ldots,u_Q}
 \sum_{r=0}^{Q-1}\sum_{i=1}^{m}|\lambda_{u_ri}|\le1,
$$
where the maximum is over full rooted paths. This is exactly the path-variation normalization in accepted fact b9989d13ba245ea2.

Use every original weight and column height:
$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{(z,t)}&=f(z|_S)e^{\lambda\cdot z}2^{-t}
 &&((z,t)\in\widehat A),\\
W&=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}w_{\mathbf I},
&p_{\mathbf I}&=w_{\mathbf I}/W.
\end{aligned}
$$
All other integer weights are zero. With the actual ambient closed-halfspace depth
$$
\tau_p(\mathbf I)=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf I}
 \sum_{\mathbf J\in H\cap\widehat A}p_{\mathbf J},
\qquad
M_3(p)=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}p_{\mathbf I}\tau_p(\mathbf I)^3,
$$
where \(H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) ranges over all closed halfspaces, one has
$$
M_3(p)\ge2^{-100}8^{-N}.
$$
The coefficient is independent of \(k,Q,m\), the chain partition, the spine, \(f\), and all field values. In particular, the multiplier can correlate all \(Q\) spine blocks arbitrarily.
